items.readable_text:
Content:
Two lines are parallel if they never meet. So, for example, the lines [MATH: r] and [MATH: s] below are parallel.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/3bb6956df43fd8fe49fe07c18b81c3e7]

Content:
If two lines are parallel, we can express this using the [MATH: \parallel] symbol as follows:

Content:
[MATH: r \parallel s]

Content:
In words, we say, "the line [MATH: r] is parallel to the line [MATH: s.]"

Content:
If two lines are not parallel, they must have a common point. In this case, we say that the lines intersect.

Content:
For example, the lines [MATH: v] and [MATH: w] below intersect at the point [MATH: P{:}]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/29479e2403661e8e7fbf8d08c1cbb1c7]

Content:
We have the following important property about lines in two-dimensional space.

Content:
> Any two distinct lines are either parallel or intersect at exactly one point.

Content:
If two lines are not parallel, they must have a common point. In this case, we say that the lines intersect.
